about: bank 1 $7000-$7FFF: the last pieces of the title banner picture, the accounting and option pages of the self test with the NVRAM bookkeeping behind them (Star Wars' TCEROM module, reworked for a byte-wide RAM image of the NVRAM), their tables, the star routines, and ROM fill

B1:712B.name: acct_page_view
B1:712B.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEACC: draws the accounting page of the self test for PHESTS (phase $4A, through L6120). turns on message $78 (the texts) and $D5, then outputs through Y in red the aux, left and right coin counts, games played and add-a-coin games, the highest wave, total coins (left plus right), total game time and total time on in seconds (the 4 second counts times 4), the average game time, play time as a percentage of time on, add-a-coin games as a percentage of games played, and the 18 bins of the game time histogram. the NVRAM image at EEROM holds whole bytes in ESB, so the values are read straight from it

B1:7389.name: coin_acct_upd
B1:7389.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEACCU, called by the coin routine every fourth interrupt (bank 0 LC6BF, through L6126): collects the top bits of the three coin counter timers S_CCTIM and compares them with EECOIN, their state at the last call. for the first counter whose bit went from 1 to 0 it adds 1 to that counter's 3-byte BCD count (RMECH, LMECH, AMECH in that order of testing) and renews the checksum of area 2. nothing is counted when area 2's checksum is bad

B1:74A7.name: time_on_upd
B1:74A7.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEUTIM: the tail of EEACCT, also called by itself from the attract mode when TIMER+2 has changed (bank 0 L6424, through L6132). reads the RAM based time TIMER with interrupts off and, if it is not lower than TIMEON in the NVRAM image, copies it to TIMEON, otherwise TIMER is put back from TIMEON. then renews the checksum of area 2, which also writes the area to the NVRAM

B1:7521.desc: checksum an EEROM area: forms the checksum of area A with ee_area_sum and stores it in the area's last byte, then writes the whole area from the RAM image at EEROM to the NVRAM, each byte as two nibbles with the high nibble first. A, X and U are preserved. bank 0 reaches it through L6138

B1:754F.name: ee_area_sum
B1:754F.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' SUMMIT: adds up the bytes of area A of the NVRAM image (start and end from T_AREA, the area's last byte is the stored checksum and is left out), starting from $11 and with the carries added back in. returns the sum in B, X pointing at the stored checksum and Z set when the two are equal. A is preserved. bank 0 reaches it through L613E

B1:7576.name: ee_init
B1:7576.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEINIT, called once by the power-on code (bank 0 LEEA4, through L6144): packs the NVRAM nibbles as they stand into the byte-wide image at EEROM, recalls the NVRAM, then checks the option area 3 and its backup, area 0. if both are bad they are loaded from the recalled NVRAM and checked again, and if they are still bad the backup is set from the option switches (EEINI0). a good one is copied over the other, areas 2 and 1 are checked, reloaded or set to defaults, the image is written to the NVRAM and TIMER is set from TIMEON

B1:75F9.name: ee_backup_opts
B1:75F9.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEINI1: copies the four bytes of the option area 3 over its backup, area 0, then goes on with the rest of ee_init - checks areas 2 and 1, loading a bad one from the NVRAM and setting it to defaults if it is still bad, writes the whole image to the NVRAM as nibbles and sets TIMER from TIMEON. opt_page_change calls it after an option has been changed

B1:765C.name: ee_area_load
B1:765C.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEINI2: loads area A of the image at EEROM from the NVRAM, packing two nibbles (high first) into each byte, the checksum byte included. A is preserved, area_end and tmp_scal are used

B1:768E.name: ee_area_check
B1:768E.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' CHKEE: checks the checksum of area A and, if it is bad, recalls the NVRAM (NOVRCL, which waits 33 frames) and loads the area from it. if it is still bad the area is set to its defaults with EECPY. called for area 2 by EEACCT, for area 1 by KE3E8, and by bank 0 through L614A

B1:76A2.name: ee_opts_check
B1:76A2.desc: called by PHIOPT when the option page is entered (bank 0 L7613, through L6150): if the checksum of the option area 3 is bad, goes through EEINI0 with A = 3, which renews that checksum, then copies the backup area 0 over area 3, rechecks areas 2 and 1 and writes the image to the NVRAM

B1:76AD.name: opt_page_view
B1:76AD.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEOPT, without the resets (they are in opt_page_change): draws the option page of the self test for PHEOPT (through L6156). turns on message $79 (the option names) and $D6, draws the value message of each of the 12 options in green, reports the NVRAM test (EETSTR), then shows in red the coin option byte OPTS0 as the switch pack 10EF and the game option byte OPTS1 as the switch pack 10D, eight letters each

B1:771A.name: vw_dip_bits
B1:771A.desc: outputs through Y a colon and the eight bits of B, bit 0 first, as letters - F for a 1, N for a 0 - then a centre instruction. uses TMPCNT

B1:773E.name: opt_page_change
B1:773E.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' EEOPT1 with the resets of EEOPT in front, called by PHEOPT every frame (through L615C): while RESETS is not 0 it shows message $D7 and on the right fire edge performs the flagged resets - high scores, accounting from the games count up, options from the option switches, NVRAM test - and clears the flags. then it draws the selected option's value in white, steps the selection with the stick (up or down past $50, 8 frames between steps) and on the left fire edge steps the selected option's value, stores it in its bit field, renews checksum and backup and draws the new value. a change of option 4, 5 or 6 (starting shields, difficulty, Jedi-letter mode) also puts the high score table back to its defaults

B1:79AC.desc: copies 4 bytes from X to U and leaves X and U as they were. the accounting page uses it to move a value of the NVRAM image to a temp, bank 0 calls it through L6168

B1:79BF.name: vw_min_sec
B1:79BF.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' TIME: outputs through Y the time in A as m:ss - the high nibble is minutes (shown as 9 at most), the low nibble counts 4 second units and is turned into BCD seconds. keeps A in sel_delay ($4C2B) meanwhile, clears BT_SUP and ends in VWBYTE

B1:7D0F.name: STARNW
B1:7D0F.desc: Star Wars' STARNW, the same instruction for instruction (the matcher missed it): new star at math RAM X. random visual x, y, z from the saved random bytes (K6511, Star Wars' RND8), y and z with the sign opposite to the current M_YPH and M_ZPH, converted to universe coordinates by MS_S1UN with ST_BIC as the block index and stored at 0, 2 and 4 of X. JVWSTAR calls it for a star that has left the view

B1:7D50.name: star_new_gnd
B1:7D50.desc: ESB's version of Star Wars' STRNWG: new ground star at math RAM X, called by JVWSTRG for a star that has left the view. visual x is 15 random bits, y the product of two of the saved random bytes with the sign opposite to the current M_YPH, z the same product. MS_S1UN with ST_BIC as the block index converts them to universe coordinates, of which x and y are stored and z is set to 0

4C20.name: opt_mask
4C20.desc: option page: the field mask of the selected option - 1, 3, 7 or 15 by its size - which is also its highest value. opt_page_change shifts it to the field's bit position when the value is changed

4C21.name: opt_desc
4C21.desc: option page: the selected option's descriptor from T_OPT - bit position in bits 7-5, field size in bits 4-3, byte number from OPTS0 in bits 2-0

4C22.name: opt_old
4C22.desc: option page: the option byte as it was, while the new field value is merged into it

4C23.name: area_end
4C23.desc: word: address in the NVRAM image where the copy loops of EECPY and ee_area_load stop

4C27.name: acc_tmp
4C27.desc: four bytes of scratch of the accounting page: the BCD value being shown - total coins in the first three, game time and time on as TMPML2 multiplies them

4C2B.name: sel_delay
4C2B.desc: option page: frames until the stick may step the selected option again, 8 after a step. vw_min_sec keeps the time byte it is showing here, and TMPML2 loads the address as the end of acc_tmp

4C2C.name: ee_tmp
4C2C.desc: scratch byte of the accounting and option pages: the average game time while it is made into minutes and seconds, the option descriptor while EEOPT3 shifts it down

4C37.name: timer_2
4C37.desc: word: third and fourth bytes of TIMER, the RAM based time on

4D01.name: dup_opts1
4D01.desc: NVRAM image, area 0: backup copy of the game option byte OPTS1. the default is the option switch byte R_OPT2 with bits 0, 3 and 4 inverted and bit 7 set

4D02.name: dup_opts2
4D02.desc: NVRAM image, area 0: backup copy of the third option byte ($4D7C, Star Wars' misc. options), 0 by default

4D03.name: EECK0
4D03.desc: CHECKSUM FOR AREA 0 (Atari's name): one byte in ESB, the last of the four bytes of the options backup

4D4C.name: potsav_1
4D4C.desc: second byte of POTSAV: the spread multiplier of the pitch pot (RHEOP+RHS_SP) saved at the end of a game

4D4D.name: potsav_2
4D4D.desc: third byte of POTSAV: the low limit of the yaw pot (RHEOY+RHS_LO)

4D4E.name: potsav_3
4D4E.desc: fourth byte of POTSAV: the spread multiplier of the yaw pot (RHEOY+RHS_SP)

4D52.name: LMECH
4D52.desc: LEFT COIN COUNT (Atari's name): 3 BCD bytes in the NVRAM image, between AMECH and RMECH

4D58.name: games_hi
4D58.desc: NVRAM image: first of the 3 BCD bytes of the number of games played, $4D58-$4D5A. Atari's GAMES sits on the middle byte in this listing

4D5A.name: games_lo
4D5A.desc: last byte of the number of games played, the one EEACCT adds 1 to

4D5B.name: cont_games
4D5B.desc: NVRAM image: 3 BCD bytes, the number of games started from the continue offer, shown as ADD-A-COIN GAMES. EEACCT adds 1 when cont_used is set

4D5F.name: ttime_1
4D5F.desc: second of the four BCD bytes of TTIME, the total game time in 4 second units

4D64.name: timeon_2
4D64.desc: word: third and fourth bytes of TIMEON

4D77.name: hist_last
4D77.desc: last of the 18 one-byte BCD bins of HISTOG: games of 5:40 and longer. the other bins are 20 seconds wide

4D78.name: high_wave
4D78.desc: NVRAM image: the highest wave reached in any game, BCD (Star Wars' ENDGAM). EEACCT raises it to wave_bcd, the accounting page shows it. it is the last data byte of area 2

4D79.name: EECK2
4D79.desc: CHECKSUM FOR AREA 2 (Atari's name): one byte in ESB, after the accounting data

4D7B.name: OPTS1
4D7B.desc: GAME MODE OPTIONS (Atari's name), the second byte of option area 3 in the NVRAM image: bits 1-0 starting shields (2 to 5), bits 3-2 play difficulty, bits 5-4 Jedi-letter mode, bit 6 music in attract, bit 7 set by the default. the option page changes the fields, the default is the option switch byte R_OPT2 with bits 0, 3 and 4 inverted

4D7D.name: EECK3
4D7D.desc: CHECKSUM FOR AREA 3 (Atari's name): one byte in ESB, after the three option bytes. ee_init compares it with EECK0

esb_notes.B1:73D9: ESB works on whole bytes of the NVRAM image and adds a count of the games started from the continue offer (cont_used, cont_games). the histogram has one BCD byte a bin. the loop that halves the bins when one reaches 100 tests U, which it does not step, so as written it does not end (K747A-K7489)
esb_notes.B1:74D7: in ESB area 0 takes R_OPT1 as read and R_OPT2 with bits 0, 3 and 4 inverted and bit 7 set, area 1 is filled by KE47D with the default high score table, area 2 comes from T_DFLT, and an area number of 3 or more only gets its checksum renewed. EECKSM, which every path ends in, also writes the area to the NVRAM
esb_notes.B1:78C6: in ESB the test runs between the byte-wide image at EEROM and the NVRAM itself, which is what EEBUF addresses here: the complement of the image is written to the NVRAM as nibbles, stored, cleared and recalled, complemented in place, stored again and compared with the image by EECMP, then cleared, recalled and compared once more. on a mismatch (K7932) NVADDR gets the NVRAM address of the nibble, NVTSTR is $FF and the image is written to the NVRAM again
esb_notes.B1:790C: in ESB this compares each byte of the image at EEROM with its two nibbles in the NVRAM (EEBUF), up to the end of the image at ST_QU
esb_notes.B1:79AE: in ESB the image at EEROM holds whole bytes: this copies A bytes from X to U and then moves both pointers back by 4, which restores them only for the 4 bytes of EETMP2. the loop ends when the count reaches 0, so A is the number of bytes
esb_notes.B1:7AE7: ESB sets the star colour by the Jedi force: white normally, purple while jedi_on is set, and purple and white in turn on bit 3 of jedi_time once less than $60 of it is left. the brightness is ST_BRT as before
esb_notes.B1:7C0F: in ESB the ground stars are not green: they are white at full brightness, or purple under the same Jedi force test as in JVWSTAR. stars out of view are regenerated with star_new_gnd (K7D50), ESB's STRNWG

questions: B1:74F1 LDX #K79A0: the operand is not the code address K79A0 inside NOVRCL but T_DFLT ($79EB) - $4B, the default table based so that the area's start offset indexes it. the listing should print it as T_DFLT-$4B

B1:7477-7489: when a histogram bin reaches 100 the halving loop loads U with HISTOG, steps X (still at the full bin) and tests U against $4D78, so it never ends and halves memory upward from that bin. Star Wars' loop used X for both. it looks like a slip in ESB that needs 100 games in one bin to show - not verified by running it

B1:7D87-7D8E: eight bytes ($02 $BB $5A $30 $5F $EE $05 $A8) between the end of star_new_gnd and the ROM fill, read by no code I found. not code ($02 is no 6809 opcode). possibly what trims the ROM checksum or signature

GD_TWL = $4D78: a false match, as 01_reconcile suspected - the byte is the highest wave on record (Star Wars' ENDGAM). this file drops the symbol with sw_drop_symbols and names the byte high_wave. if a notes file may not drop a symbol, the ram entry 4D78 has to go and the comment at B1:716B stays wrong

GAMES = $4D59 is the middle byte of the 3-byte games count $4D58-$4D5A (the vote came from LDX #GAMES-2, which in Star Wars' nibble layout is one byte back and here is $4D57). this file names $4D58 games_hi and $4D5A games_lo and leaves GAMES alone. moving GAMES to $4D58 would be cleaner

sw_drop_comments B1:7406 and B1:7429: the wrong carried text there is the standalone line INC TOTAL TIME ON COUNT above each address, not an inline comment - the code counts games played and continued games. if the generator cannot drop a standalone line, the two new comments still stand beside it

T_DFLT (B1:79EB-7A18): the listing shows it as $80 bytes, a zero byte and .word rows with Star Wars' comments (HIGHEST WAVE LEVEL ATTAINED at K7A12, CHECKSUM FOR AREA 2 at K7A18). in ESB it is 46 single bytes for $4D4B-$4D78, and K7A19 is one unused zero byte before T_OPT. the label T_DFLT at K79EB falls on the row after EEMASK

the labels bnr_back_a (B1:7014), bnr_back_c (B1:7056) and bnr_back_k (B1:70C0) fall inside .byte rows. that the last four letter pieces spell BACK is read from the shapes only (piece 22 at K6F73 has two inner outlines, 23 one, 24 and 25 none) - I did not render them
$4802 is used as a byte counter at B1:760F-7615 and B1:77A7-77AD (Star Wars used TMPCNT). the address has the names TMPLIN and TMPTP2 of other routines in the defines, so it is not named here

$4C2B has three uses: the stick repeat delay of the option page (named sel_delay for it), the temp of vw_min_sec, and as an address the end of acc_tmp in TMPML2 (LDX #$4C2B at B1:737B, which should read acc_tmp+4)
bank 0 L6369 comments its call of EETMP2 as moving NVRAM nibbles to bytes: in ESB EETMP2 is a plain 4-byte copy from the byte-wide image
which fire switch bit $40 of GN_SWE is has no symbol in the ESB defines (Star Wars' RFIRBT), the comment at B1:774A calls it right fire after message $D7
OPTS1 bit 7: Star Wars' T_OPT comment calls it freeze mode, not usable from the option page. ESB's default always sets it and the 10D display always shows it as F. what tests it was not looked for
